Respond with ONLY this JSON (no markdown fence, no preamble, no trailing prose):
{"claims": [{"axis": "correctness"|"simplicity"|"robustness", "position": "pro"|"con", "text": "one specific factual sentence"}, ...]}

# ATN SECRET-ALLOWANCE + TRIPWIRE — Canonical Design (owner review)

## Executive summary (end state)
Each agent runs in its own PID; the daemon computes a fractal, monotonically-narrowing secrets allowance at spawn (`L_child = resolve_spec(requested) ∩ L_parent`) and, at PID-bind, mints an owner-secret-gated broker nonce carrying that allowance and registers `{child_pid → policies}` with the unchanged kevin vault-broker. The worker then calls `secret_*` tools from its OWN PID; the broker authorizes by kernel PID and stages values to nameless files, returning only `{var_name, path}` — the value never enters model context or daemon memory. A daemon-level `SecurityMonitor` holds only a LIVE-exposure set (fed at stage, drained at revoke + TTL), scans `STEP_OUTPUT`, and emits `SECURITY_ALARM` (names-only, `source_agent` only, no `agent_id` key). Every gate is fail-closed: broker down / no grant / unknown service / isolation-off / missing monitor → deny; the monitor never holds a standing vault copy.
